newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARINERS SEND JOSE CRUZ JR TO BLUE JAYS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARINERS SEND JOSE CRUZ JR TO BLUE JAYS.

text.p: The Seattle Mariners, in an attempt to bolster baseball's worst bullpen, sent highly touted prospect Jose Cruz Jr to the Toronto Blue Jays for relievers Mike Timlin and Paul Spoljaric on Thursday.
Cruz, a switch-hitting outfielder, is hitting .269 with 12 homers and 34 RBI in 48 games as a rookie.

The 23-year-old son of former Houston Astros outfielder Jose Cruz was expected to solidify the Mariners' left field spot for years to come. But Seattle parted with him to get desperately needed relief pitching ahead of the midnight trade deadline.
"We needed to bolster our bullpen and were able to go out and get two proven relievers in Mike Timlin and Paul Spoljaric," said Woody Woodward, the Mariners vice president of baseball operations.
"We hated to trade a fine, young talent in Jose Cruz Jr, but in order to give us the best shot at an American League pennant, we had to trade quality to get quality."
Timlin, a 31-year-old right-hander, is 3-2 with nine saves and a 2.87 ERA in 38 relief appearances. He should replace Norm Charlton and Bobby Ayala as the Mariners' closer.
Charlton and Ayala have combined for 20 saves, but have blown 11 for Seattle, which leads second-place Anaheim by just a half game in the AL West.
Spoljaric, a 26-year-old left-hander is 0-3 with three saves and a 3.19 ERA in 37 games, allowing just 37 hits while striking out 43 in 48 innings.

"There's been a lot of discussion over the past couple of weeks about our needing some offence," Toronto general manager Gord Ash said. "Jose Cruz Jr is going to give us offence immediately and in the future. ... He's an excellent offensive player. He's got power, he can hit for average. He also can play defence."
